notes: Check batch 2026-11-05-check-3 (previous sweep 2026-10-31-b at 74112b4): four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. Each result.json records head 9a47da2 with uncommitted changes and skill_hash 558f46e4..., which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the current idiomatic-elixir/ folder (the working tree, including the uncommitted SKILL.md edit), and every transcript contains the new with-rule sentence "whose failure already has the shape the function returns". skills_listed is 40 for every run. Haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 read SKILL.md only; sonnet-2 also read references/library-design.md, so Expected reads (none) is met in all four. In the scratch folder all four pass mix format --check-formatted and run against Decimal compiled from a local deps copy. A probe gave correct per-currency totals, correct last-order dates (including a row with a -02:00 offset that crosses midnight UTC), the top five with ties broken by customer id, and empty results for []; every run returns {:error, ...} for a missing key, a bad amount, an amount with trailing text, an unknown status and a bad date. Haiku-1 raises FunctionClauseError for a non-string amount because parse_amount/1 hands it straight to Decimal.parse/1, as haiku-1 and haiku-2 did in 2026-10-31-b; no listed rule covers it.

Rules changed since 74112b4 (git diff 74112b4 -- idiomatic-elixir/, which includes the uncommitted SKILL.md edit), graded against the current text. On this case's list four rules changed. The with rule now says "Give each step a private function whose failure already has the shape the function returns, `{:error, reason}` for a function that returns tuples, `:error` for a fetch, `nil` for a lookup that returns a value or `nil`, and let `with` pass it through unchanged" and "when that call does not return `{:ok, value}`, the `case` goes in a small private function"; every step helper in the four runs returns {:error, reason}, and no run nests a case inside a with, so these sentences decide no verdict. The Enum/Map rule gained the row `Enum.find(pairs, fn {_k, v} -> f(v) end)` followed by a `case` that takes `k` out | `Enum.find_value(...)`; no run calls Enum.find. The `do:` rule now says "The one wrap to keep is a function head that `mix format` breaks after a long guard" and "Put the value being checked on the left of `==`"; no run wraps a do: body, and every == (the &(&1.status == :completed) captures) has the checked value on the left. The `->` rule gained "when the success row calls on, as `{:ok, bytes} -> hash_if_canonical(token, bytes)` does beside `_other -> :error`, the clauses are not a table and every body goes below"; the inline cases in haiku-1 (91-93, 99-100) and haiku-2 (119-121, 127-129, 135-136) have success rows that return {:ok, value}, so they stay clean. Outside the list, Match every expected shape gained "Different failures need different reasons too"; every run returns distinct reasons for a missing key and a bad field, so nothing is listed under it.

Verdicts worth checking. With, sonnet-1 lines 106-112 pipe the reduce_while result into a case whose clauses are {:ok, orders} -> {:ok, Enum.reverse(orders)} and {:error, _reason} = error -> error; the sentence "A `case` whose error clause is `{:error, _reason} = error -> error` is the same pass-through spelled out over four lines; write it as the `with`" is unchanged since 74112b4 and decided the identical lines in 2026-10-30-check-2's sonnet-1, so it is violated here; the pipe into case itself is held clean under the pipeline rule as that grade held it. Inline `->`: fn clauses are measured from pattern to body, as 2026-10-31-b measured them; the longest are 66 characters (haiku-1 line 143, sonnet-2 line 167, the latter identical to the 2026-10-31-b opus-1 line held clean at 66), and haiku-2 line 119 (66, with a guard) is the shape that grade held clean in opus-1. Name a step: tagged literals of plain variables {:ok, / %Order{ ... }} (sonnet-1 124-131, sonnet-2 118-125) are held clean as data, as in 2026-10-31-b. Sonnet-1 lines 86-90 are a different shape that grade did not meet: {:ok, %{customers: customer_summaries(orders), top_customers: top_customers(orders)}} spread over five lines by mix format, the case the rule opens with ("When `mix format` spreads an expression over several lines"). It is held clean because the two calls are siblings in a map, not one step feeding another as in the rule's binary_part/strip_comments example, and the rule says "Length alone decides nothing"; 2026-10-31-b's sonnet-2 bound the same map as report before {:ok, report}, which would be the fix if the rule is meant to cover this shape. Lists, Enum/Map: length(completed) and Enum.count(completed) on a list also used elsewhere are counts, held clean as before. Other rules: haiku-2's Order struct has no @type t (listed under the struct rule as 2026-10-31-b listed the same shape) and its build/1 @doc has no ## Examples (listed under the documentation rule as 2026-10-31-b listed the same gap in all four baseline runs other than opus-1; every 2026-10-31-b skill run had examples); haiku-1 and sonnet-2 match the five required keys in a multi-line head with a catch-all clause below, held clean under the head rule as earlier grades held it, and sonnet-2's = _row alias is not a bound field.
